summary: Segmented control is a row of two to five choices where exactly one is picked, shown as a raised knob that slides to it. Use it to switch between views of the same thing, like a day, a week and a month, or to set one option from a few. It sits inline next to a title and changes what's below it at once.
use: When people switch between a few views of the same content, like Day, Week and Month.
When there are two to five short options and all of them should stay visible.
When the change should happen at once, without a separate Apply.
Not for more than five options, or long labels: use a select or tabs with an overflow then.
features: `options` are the choices, each with a `value` and a `label`. The picked one sits on a raised knob that slides and resizes to it.
`as="tabs"` (the default) makes it a tab list for switching a panel; `as="radio"` makes it a radio group for setting an option.
`id` ties the tabs to their panel: the panel takes `id="<id>-panel"` and `aria-labelledby="<id>-<value>"`.

The demo switches the pricing launch between a day of events, a working week with each weekday's first event and a count of the rest, and a month with a dot on each busy day. Previous and next step a day, a week or a month at a time, Today comes back to the current date, and a day in the week or the month opens it in the day view. The range above the panel crossfades as it changes.
a11y: As tabs it is a `tablist` named by `label`, each option a `tab` with `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`, and the panel a `tabpanel` labelled by the picked tab.
As a radio group it is a `radiogroup` with `radio` options and `aria-checked`.
Only the picked option is in the tab order. ← and → move and pick, wrapping at the ends, and Home and End jump to the first and last.
The knob is decoration; the picked option's state says the same.
In the demo, previous and next are named for the view, like Previous week, and each day in the week and the month is a button named with its date and how many events it has.

faq.q: Should it be tabs or a radio group?
faq.a: Tabs when it changes what a panel shows, like a calendar view. A radio group when it sets a value that's saved or sent, like a billing period.

faq.q: Can an option have an icon?
faq.a: Yes. `label` takes JSX, so put an icon before the text, or only an icon with an `aria-label` inside it.

faq.q: Does the knob slide when the labels change width?
faq.a: Yes. It measures the picked option whenever the control resizes, so it follows a translated label or a new font.

faq.q: How many options can it take?
faq.a: It works best with two to five short ones. Past that, the options get narrow on a phone.
